plan.headline: Cloud Access Abuse and Exploit Scanning

overview.text: Access itself was a commodity in two reports published this week, although they described separate operations.
Mandiant’s account of LLMJacking described intruders using enterprise access to language models across several providers.
The financial consequence can arrive quickly: fraudulent cloud charges may rise sharply within hours, rather than building through the slower consumption associated with cryptojacking.
The incidents described occurred during 2026; their publication this week does not place all of that activity inside this reporting window.
The distinction between reporting and event dates also matters for XCPE: Google’s account placed the disruption in the week before publication.
The backdoor had drawn more than 1.3 million set-top boxes into a botnet before Google and industry partners dismantled it.
Its monetization extended beyond the original operator: access was sold to criminal affiliates, and their malware modules were loaded onto infected devices.
The SSH reporting offered a narrower signal: SANS saw increased attempts against Sshole in its Cowrie honeypots.
That is evidence of activity in a limited observation set, rather than a measure of global attack frequency or proof that intruders succeeded.
Long passwords stood out from the usual brute-force traffic, but the sensors recorded only the first 255 characters.
Taken together, these accounts distinguish documented misuse of existing access, a reported botnet disruption, and a qualified signal of exploit attempts; they do not establish a shared campaign.

summary.text: Mandiant’s cases span several cloud and model providers, with rapid fraudulent billing as the immediate financial consequence.
The reported disruption affected a backdoor whose operator sold access and loaded affiliates’ malware onto devices.
SANS’s password-length collection limit qualifies what its honeypots can show about the observed attempts.

plan.headline: LLM Hijacking Can Drive Rapid Cloud Bills

overview.text: Enterprise access to language models can become a fast-moving financial liability when it is hijacked.
Mandiant described multiple LLMJacking incidents across cloud and model providers, with fraudulent charges capable of climbing sharply within hours.
That speed distinguishes the abuse from the more gradual resource consumption of cryptojacking.
For cloud teams, unexpected model-related charges are a concrete reason to investigate possible misuse of enterprise access.
Google and industry partners also dismantled the XCPE backdoor, which had enrolled more than 1.3 million set-top boxes.
The operator sold access to criminal affiliates and loaded their malware modules onto infected devices.
The disruption targeted a business that turned control of those devices into a service for criminal affiliates.

summary.text: Cases included financial services, retail, technology and transportation organizations across North America, South America and Asia Pacific.
Google assessed with high confidence that Videostrong Technology Co. developed, deployed and operated the backdoor for financial gain.
Long SSH passwords stood out in SANS’s Cowrie honeypots as attempts to exploit Sshole increased.
